# Genesis Apocryphon Column 2 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Genesis Apocryphon Column 2 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 2:1 — "was afraid" vs "was overcome with fear"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "was-afraid" | Bare literal with hyphenation |
| LOGOS | "was afraid" | Standard formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "was overcome with fear" | Dynamic expansion for emotional intensity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "was afraid." PNEUMA's expansion is unwarranted by the Aramaic dechelat; EMET's hyphenation is unnecessary.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:3 — "Ages" vs "Eternity" — rendering of 'almayya

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-King of-all the-Ages" | Literal plural of 'alam |
| LOGOS | "the King of all the Ages" | Formal equivalent preserving plural |
| PNEUMA | "the King of all Eternity" | Dynamic singular abstract |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "the King of all the Ages." The Aramaic 'almayya is plural and should be rendered as such; PNEUMA's singular "Eternity" collapses the plural.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:5 — "lies" vs "falsehood"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "without lies" | Direct literal |
| LOGOS | "without falsehood" | Elevated formal register |
| PNEUMA | "without any lies" | Dynamic with intensifier |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "without falsehood." More dignified register appropriate to an oath context.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:8 — "is from" vs "was fathered by"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "this child is [from] the Watchers" | Literal with preposition |
| LOGOS | "this child is from the Watchers" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "this child was fathered by the Watchers" | Dynamic interpretation making paternity explicit |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS "this child is from the Watchers." PNEUMA's "fathered by" is too specific an interpretation of the Aramaic min ("from").

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 2:11 — "great force" vs "great vehemence" vs "fierce intensity"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "with great force" | Literal rendering of betoqupa rabba |
| LOGOS | "with great vehemence" | Formal rendering with elevated register |
| PNEUMA | "with fierce intensity" | Dynamic paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "with great vehemence." Better captures the emotional quality of speech than EMET's physical "force," while avoiding PNEUMA's overly free rendering.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:13-14 — Bitenosh's intimate appeal

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the time-of-love / and the gasping-of my-breath in-my-bosom" | Hyphenated construct chains |
| LOGOS | "the time of love / and the gasping of my breath within my breast" | Formal with "breast" for Aramaic chadya |
| PNEUMA | "the tender moments of our love / and how I gasped with pleasure in your embrace" | Free dynamic paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. "Within my breast" preserves the Aramaic body-language; PNEUMA's "gasped with pleasure in your embrace" over-interprets the text far beyond what the Aramaic supports.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:18 — "face" vs "countenance" vs "expression"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "my face had-changed" | Literal with hyphenation |
| LOGOS | "my countenance had changed" | Formal elevated register |
| PNEUMA | "my expression had changed" | Modern dynamic equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "my countenance had changed." "Countenance" is the traditional biblical rendering and suits the text's register.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:19 — "controlled" vs "restrained" vs "mastered"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "she controlled her anger" | Literal rendering |
| LOGOS | "she restrained her anger" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "she mastered her anger" | Dynamic with connotation of struggle |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "she restrained her anger." "Restrained" conveys both the effort and the result.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:23 — "planting of this fruit" — conception idiom

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the planting-of this fruit" | Literal with hyphenated construct |
| LOGOS | "the planting of this fruit" | Formal equivalent preserving metaphor |
| PNEUMA | "you are the one who planted this fruit in me" | Dynamic paraphrase making meaning explicit |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "the planting of this fruit." The Aramaic netsibat pirya is a fixed idiom for conception; PNEUMA's paraphrase dissolves the idiom into explanation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:26 — "distorted" vs "disfigured" vs "twisted"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "changed and distorted" | Literal pair |
| LOGOS | "changed and disfigured" | Formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "changed and twisted" | Dynamic equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "changed and disfigured." "Disfigured" better captures the visible alteration of facial features than either alternative.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

*Total disagreements: 10*
*Resolution: LOGOS 8, EMET/LOGOS 1, Compromise 0, EMET 0, PNEUMA 0, Split 1*
